back: The rule that a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
notes: the boy runs / the boys run

front: Phrases that do not change the subject
back: of ..., as well as, together with, along with, including, in addition to.
notes: The price of books has risen.

back: The verb agrees with the subject nearer to it.
notes: Neither the coach nor the players were ready.

back: each, every, everyone, everybody, everything, someone, somebody, anyone, nobody, no one, nothing.
notes: Each of the boys has a pen.

back: both, few, many, several; police, cattle, people, clothes, trousers, scissors.
news, mathematics, physics, economics, measles; amounts such as 'ten dollars' or 'five kilometres' seen as one total.

front: a number of vs the number of
back: A number of (several) takes a plural verb; the number of (the figure) takes a singular verb.
notes: A number of boys were late. The number of boys has fallen.

back: Singular verb when the group acts as one unit, plural when you think of the members; keep pronouns consistent with the verb.
notes: The team has won its match / The team are arguing among themselves.

back: The subject is one, so the verb is singular.
notes: One of my friends lives in Kwekwe.

back: The subject comes after the verb, so look ahead: there is + singular, there are + plural.
